Comments and string literals are scrubbed (stripCommentsAndStrings) and brace-matched bodies extracted (extractBracedBody) before member/call scanning; the scrub preserves byte length and newline positions, so lines counted over the scrubbed text still match the source. The member regexes end at the opening paren, so declSignature scans on from the match with paren depth to the terminating { or ; and Signature carries the full parameter list, mutability/visibility and returns clause; before that it stopped at the paren. StartLine is the declaration's own line: leading whitespace in the declaration regexes can no longer cross a line boundary, members are anchored on the contract's opening brace rather than its match start, and buildImportEntities sets a line on import entities, which previously reported 0 (#6040). Proven by the extractor_test.go and line_attribution_test.go suites (contract/library/interface discovery, member CONTAINS, signature capture, reported lines). Contract-level state variables are emitted as SCOPE.Schema (subtype field) named <Contract>.<var>, with the full declaration text in Signature and a CONTAINS edge from the owning contract (#6135). findStateVariables recognises them structurally: a statement terminated by ';' at brace depth zero of the contract body, which excludes function locals and struct/enum members with no indentation heuristic, plus a leading-token filter that drops the other depth-zero forms (bodiless interface functions, event/error declarations, using-for and type directives). Every state variable is emitted whatever its visibility, with visibility and mutability carried in Signature; no getter is synthesised for public ones because the source does not declare one. Known miss: function-type state variables, which open with the `function` keyword. Emission is only half the story: until #6138 the indexer's file fold (foldFileComponentDuplicates) deleted any class-like SCOPE.Component whose name matched its file stem, and "interface" is in classLikeComponentSubtypes while "contract" and "library" are not — so on @openzeppelin/contracts@5.2.0 42 of 61 interfaces never reached the document while all 71 contracts and 45 libraries did, and the dropped interface took its Signature (and with it the `is ...` inheritance clause) along with it. The fold now applies only where a module and its exported declaration are the same entity, so every contract, library and interface the extractor emits survives to the graph.
